title: I Claude-coded a Slavic folk-horror dicebuilder roguelike in Godot — trailer + free demo
author: Jiggzawyr
selftext:
**Horn & Dice** — a dark folkloric roguelike where dice *are* the build. Roll, reroll, and resolve across runs, rooted in Slavic mythology.

  
Free demo + Steam page: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4971770/Horn\_\_Dice/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4971770/Horn__Dice/)

Built solo with following AI tools:

* **Engine:** Godot 4.7 / GDScript
* **Code:** Claude
* **Art:** Gemini
* **SFX:** ElevenLabs
* **Music:** OpenMusicAI

comments.author: UpDown
comments.body: I have a question about using AI in godot. I moved away from Godot because I thought AI would have difficulty interacting with UI based game development, so I am using code-only LOVE2d. But it seems maybe that has changed and AI is working better with software like godot, unity, etc. What exactly are you doing to use AI in godot?

replies.author: Jiggzawyr
replies.body: It has changed. I rememeber AI being bad with Godot, it could not get syntax right for files that are usually genereted using Godot UI. Now it gets everyting right. I just connect Claude Code to folder where my Godot project is it does almost everything. From writing GDScript code to arranging Godot scenes. i had to give him 2d assets for him to use. I used Gemini to generate PNG files. Then edited them in Photoshop before giving them to it. It does happend that something does not work at first. Code does not behave like i asked. But it is able to fix everything after explicitly asking to fix what i think he got wrong. Overall i would say it is good enough for game development in Godot.
